Note::TexAccessor::dedup_blank_lines¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::dedup_blank_lines() const

Cap Vertical Whitespace Without Reflowing Source¶

dedup_blank_lines() reduces every run of two or more blank lines to one blank line. In byte terms, three or more consecutive line-ending sequences, with optional spaces or tabs on the intervening empty lines, become exactly two line endings. The first ends the preceding content line; the second is the single retained blank line.

A blank line may be empty or contain only horizontal ASCII whitespace. Spaces and tabs on a collapsed blank run are removed. Content-line indentation, single line endings, and an already singular blank line remain untouched. The method does not trim the document, wrap text, collapse ordinary spaces, or interpret TeX environments; it is intentionally narrower than fix_linebreaks().

LF (\n), CRLF (\r\n), and CR (\r) are all recognized. Deduplication preserves the original line-ending bytes of the two retained boundaries; it does not silently convert CRLF to LF. Use line_norm() when a uniform LF representation is required, and choose the order deliberately: normalize then deduplicate for canonical LF output, or deduplicate alone to retain the source convention.

Each Text cell is processed independently. The result is a newly allocated Note with the same rank and shape; empty cells, cells without excess blank lines, and undefined state are preserved. Native non-Text dtypes reject. The kernel scans each byte once and reserves at most the original byte count, so its working cost is linear without per-line container allocation.

Example 1: Collapse An LF Run¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note("alpha\n\n\n\nbeta");
std::cout << source.tex().dedup_blank_lines() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"alpha\n\nbeta"

Example 2: Whitespace-Only Blank Lines¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note("one\n  \n\t\n\n\ntwo");
std::cout << source.tex().dedup_blank_lines() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"one\n\ntwo"

Example 3: CRLF Is Preserved¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note("one\r\n \r\n\t\r\ntwo");
std::cout << source.tex().dedup_blank_lines() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"one\r\n\r\ntwo"

Example 4: Batched Shape And Stable Cells¶

const auto spaced = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{"alpha\n\n\n\nbeta", "one\r\n \r\n\t\r\ntwo",
                             "already\n\ncompact", "single line"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto compact = spaced.tex().dedup_blank_lines();
std::cout << compact << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["alpha\n\nbeta", "one\r\n\r\ntwo"], 
  ["already\n\ncompact", "single line"]
]

Example 5: Compose With Newline Normalization¶

const auto canonical =
    pluss::make_note("one\r\n \r\n\t\r\ntwo")
        .tex().line_norm().tex().dedup_blank_lines();
std::cout << canonical << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"one\n\ntwo"

Example 6: Undefined And Invalid Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().dedup_blank_lines().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().dedup_blank_lines();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "blank lines Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
blank lines Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • line_norm: convert CRLF and CR endings to LF.

  • fix_linebreaks: perform broader line-ending and trailing-space cleanup.

  • Note::collapse_whitespace: collapse all ASCII whitespace rather than preserving document lines.
